comments.author: @manekinskajloker7589
comments.text:
To be fair, these cities have much deeper Slavic and Polish roots than people often acknowledge.

Gdańsk was known by its Polish name long before the modern German spelling “Danzig” became established. It was the Free City of Gdańsk between 1920 and 1939, and Nazi Germany annexed it in 1939. So its history is more complicated than simply calling it a German city.

The same goes for Wrocław, historically known in German as Breslau. And Szczecin, known in German as Stettin, also has Slavic roots mainly with Poland itself not Germany. The exact origin of its name is debated, but one theory links it to an old Slavic word associated with a hilltop.

These cities have a long and complex history involving Polish, Slavic, German and other influences. But their Slavic roots didn't suddenly appear after World War II, and their Polish names aren't simply modern inventions. 😅
